site_description: Emanuele Mason — systems thinker. Energy platform engineering at Enersem, with a research background in multi-agent AI and water resource management.
meta_portfolio_description: Projects by Emanuele Mason: the Enersem EMS platform and LM Deck Tools, plus research on multi-agent negotiation, water systems and river erosion.
meta_biography_description: How Emanuele Mason got here: environmental engineering, water resource management, a PhD in multi-agent reinforcement learning, and building an energy platform at Enersem.
meta_library_description: Selected publications by Emanuele Mason in Water Resources Research and JWRPM, plus the AAMAS 2016 best paper award.
hero_subhead: I build software for energy monitoring at Enersem, with a research background in AI and water systems before that. Outside of work I practice Tai Chi and Shaolin, fence with sabers and other swords sometimes, and mostly just try to get a little better at things, slowly.
project_ems_blurb: Cloud platform for industrial energy monitoring. I've helped build it since 2018, from early prototype to what runs in production today.
project_decktools_blurb: A local-first Magic: The Gathering collection manager — no accounts, no servers, your data stays on your device.
project_dmmt_blurb: Program to code equations of dynamic models and simulate them fast. Python and C++.
project_sec_blurb: A negotiation protocol for identifying tradeoffs among conflicting objectives.
project_more_blurb: Multi-objective riverscape evolution — a study of optimality in river erosion processes, going back to my master's thesis.
project_thesis_blurb: A LaTeX thesis template for PoliMi's DEIB department, still getting the occasional fork.
project_restoration_blurb: A review of river restoration projects across Western Europe, on flood risk and ecological benefits.
bio_step1_body: Started in environmental engineering, then narrowed into water resource management — systems where you're balancing flood risk, ecology, and human use all at once, and nobody's model is ever quite right.
bio_step2_meta: Research Fellow, PoliMi · Visiting Scholar, Penn State
bio_step2_body: Spent time as a research fellow and teaching assistant at PoliMi, plus a stretch as a visiting scholar at Penn State — still listed as an alumnus of the EI@DEIB group. This is also where the "systems that need patience to understand" thread really started.
bio_step3_body: A PhD on inverse reinforcement learning and multi-agent negotiation, applied to water systems. Cum laude, eventually.
bio_step4_body: Joined Enersem as an external consultant in 2018, became a socio lavoratore in 2020, and I'm Digital Solutions Manager now. I split my time between building the EMS platform itself — architecture, cloud infrastructure, prototyping — and supervising funded research projects like TEPORE and LombHe@t.
practice_quote: I try to apply Kung Fu everywhere — to any study, practice, or pursuit that takes patience, energy, and time to complete.
practice_1_body: Patient, sustained practice beats quick wins.
practice_2_body: Don't just model it — prototype end-to-end.
practice_3_body: Open source, published research, no black boxes.
practice_4_body: Watching F1, hiking when I can, and going to rock concerts.
outside_body: I hold a black belt in Tai Chi and Shaolin (FESK-registered), and I fence with sabers and other swords at a historical fencing club. Otherwise: Formula 1 on the TV, hiking when the weather cooperates, rock concerts whenever there's one worth driving to, and whatever's on Spotify at the moment.
